admin.builtinAdmin: The built-in Administrator account is enabled.
admin.fix.linux: Do administration from a separate account: from it, remove your daily account from the group with [code]sudo gpasswd -d NAME sudo[/code], NAME being your daily account (wheel instead of sudo on Fedora/Arch).
admin.fix.mac: Create a separate administrator account (System Settings → Users & Groups → Add User…, type Administrator), log in to it once, then turn off "Allow this user to administer this computer" for your daily account. Admin prompts then take the other account's name and password.
admin.fix.nopasswd: Remove NOPASSWD (and !authenticate) from the rule with [code]sudo visudo[/code], or [code]sudo visudo -f /etc/sudoers.d/FILE[/code].
admin.fix.uac: Control Panel → User Accounts → Change User Account Control settings → at least "Notify me only when apps try to make changes to my computer (default)", then restart. If a policy sets it, ask IT.
admin.fix.win: Create a separate administrator account (Settings → Accounts → Other users → Add account, then Change account type → Administrator), sign in to it once, then change your daily account's type to Standard User. UAC then asks for the administrator's password.
admin.isAdmin: This account is an administrator ({groups}): malware you run by mistake needs only one approval to take over the whole machine.
admin.nopasswd: sudo runs every command as root without a password ({where}): any program you run can take over the machine silently.
admin.nopasswdSome: sudo runs some commands as root without a password ({where}); many commands can be abused to get a root shell.
admin.note.sudo: Could not ask sudo which rules apply ({err}).
admin.note.uac: Could not read the User Account Control settings.
admin.note.unknown: Could not tell whether this account is an administrator.
admin.pass.allowed: This account is an administrator, which the policy allows.
admin.pass.standard: This account is a standard user.
admin.uacNoPrompt: UAC elevates administrators without asking (ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin = 0): any program can take administrator rights silently.
admin.uacOff: User Account Control is turned off (EnableLUA = 0): programs run with full administrator rights without asking.
ai.fix: Keep tokens out of MCP configs: reference an environment variable instead ([code]"env": {"API_KEY": "${env:API_KEY}"}[/code] or the agent's own input/secret mechanism) and load it from the OS keychain ([code]touchenv run[/code] on macOS). Turn approvals and the sandbox back on: a prompt injection in any file, web page or issue the agent reads can then run commands as you.

backup.fix.mac.encrypt: System Settings → General → Time Machine → select the disk → Remove Disk, then Add Backup Disk again with "Encrypt backup" turned on (on recent macOS an existing backup cannot be encrypted in place, so the disk is erased).
backup.fix.mac.findMy: System Settings → your name (Apple Account) → iCloud → Find My Mac → turn it on.
backup.fix.mac.setup: System Settings → General → Time Machine → Add Backup Disk, with "Encrypt backup" turned on, or ask IT how this Mac should be backed up.
backup.fix.mac.stale: Connect the backup disk, then Time Machine in the menu bar → Back Up Now.
backup.fix.win.findMy: Settings → Privacy & security → Find my device → turn it on (it needs a Microsoft account and location services).
backup.none: No backup is set up: a lost or broken laptop takes its files with it.
backup.noneAllowed: No Time Machine backup is set up (the policy does not require one).

cracked.fix: Uninstall the cracked software and any crack or activation tool, remove the lines the crack added to the hosts file, and run a full malware scan: cracks often carry information stealers. If the scan finds one, change the passwords and tokens used on this machine. Ask IT for a licensed copy.
cracked.fixAlternatives: Uninstall the cracked software and any crack or activation tool, remove the lines the crack added to the hosts file, and run a full malware scan: cracks often carry information stealers. If the scan finds one, change the passwords and tokens used on this machine. Ask IT for a licensed copy, or use a free, open-source alternative from ArtCraft (https://getartcraft.com).

firewall.linux.fix: Ubuntu/Debian: [code]sudo ufw enable[/code] (it blocks incoming connections and allows outgoing). Fedora/RHEL/openSUSE: [code]sudo systemctl enable --now firewalld[/code].
firewall.linux.inputDrops: The firewall drops incoming connections by default (input policy).
firewall.linux.noDrop: No firewall drops incoming connections: no nftables or iptables input chain defaults to drop.
firewall.linux.noneNoUfw: No firewall is on: ufw is not installed, and no firewalld, nftables or iptables service is running. (If you load rules some other way, [code]sudo bordercheck -only firewall[/code] checks them.)
firewall.linux.noneUfwOff: No firewall is on: ufw is installed but off, and no firewalld, nftables or iptables service is running. (If you load rules some other way, [code]sudo bordercheck -only firewall[/code] checks them.)
firewall.linux.rootOnly: The {services} service loads firewall rules, but they can only be read as root, so BorderCheck cannot tell whether they block incoming connections. Run [code]sudo bordercheck -only firewall[/code] to check them.
firewall.linux.unknown: Could not tell without root: there is no ufw configuration and systemd did not say which firewall services run. Run [code]sudo bordercheck -only firewall[/code] to check the rules.
firewall.linux.zone.fix: [code]sudo firewall-cmd --set-default-zone=public[/code] (allows SSH and DHCPv6 only); open what you need with [code]--add-service[/code].
firewall.linux.zoneOpenPorts: firewalld is on, but its default zone {zone} lets in every port from 1025 to 65535.
firewall.linux.zoneTrusted: firewalld is on, but its default zone {zone} lets everything in.
firewall.mac.off.fix: System Settings → Network → Firewall → turn it on. Or: [code]sudo /usr/libexec/ApplicationFirewall/socketfilterfw --setglobalstate on[/code]
firewall.mac.onStealth: Firewall and stealth mode are on.
firewall.mac.stealthOff: The firewall is on, but stealth mode is off: this Mac answers probes from the network.
firewall.mac.stealthOff.fix: System Settings → Network → Firewall → Options → turn on stealth mode. Or: [code]sudo /usr/libexec/ApplicationFirewall/socketfilterfw --setstealthmode on[/code]
firewall.win.off.fix: Windows Security → Firewall & network protection → turn it on for every network. Or, as administrator: [code]Set-NetFirewallProfile -All -Enabled True[/code]
firewall.win.on: Windows Firewall is on for every profile.

listeners.fix: Bind dev servers to 127.0.0.1 (Vite: drop [code]--host[/code]; Docker: [code]-p 127.0.0.1:PORT:PORT[/code]) and quit what you don't need. To share something, use a Cloudflare Tunnel instead of an open port.

listeners.infoOnly.other: {n} ports can be reached from other machines, all held by well-known services (such as AirPlay Receiver, Dropbox LAN sync or Windows' own system services): listed for information, nothing to fix.

mesh.allowed: Allowed by policy to accept incoming connections: {tools}.
mesh.blocked: {tool} is connected and blocks incoming connections.
mesh.connUnknown: {tool} is running; which networks it has joined could not be read without admin rights.
mesh.fix.hamachi: Hamachi cannot refuse incoming connections: leave the networks you do not need, go offline in Hamachi when you are not using it, or uninstall it.
mesh.fix.nebula: Remove the rules under firewall.inbound in Nebula's config that this computer does not need; with none, Nebula lets no connection in.
mesh.fix.netbird: Turn on NetBird's "Block inbound connections": [code]netbird up --block-inbound[/code]. Or disconnect ([code]netbird down[/code]) when you do not need it.
mesh.fix.wireguard: WireGuard cannot refuse incoming connections itself: deactivate tunnels you do not need, and make sure the computer's firewall also filters the tunnel's interface.
mesh.fix.zerotier: ZeroTier cannot refuse incoming connections on the computer itself: leave networks you do not need ([code]sudo zerotier-cli leave[/code] with the network ID), make sure the computer's firewall also filters the ZeroTier interface, and ask the network's admin to limit traffic with flow rules.
mesh.inboundUnknown: {tool} is connected; whether it blocks incoming connections could not be read without admin rights.
mesh.none: No private-network (mesh VPN) software was found.
mesh.open: {tool} is connected and does not block incoming connections: other members of its private network can reach every port this computer listens on, unless the computer's firewall stops them.
outbound.fix.mac: Install a free outbound firewall such as LuLu from Objective-See (https://objective-see.org/products/lulu.html, open source): it asks before an app connects out, so malware phoning home or a program sending your data somewhere shows up.
outbound.fix.win: Install simplewall (https://github.com/henrypp/simplewall, free and open source). Once its filters are enabled it blocks every app you have not allowed, so it will ask you to allow each app the first time it connects; then malware phoning home or a program sending your data somewhere shows up. Or ask IT to set Windows Firewall to block outgoing connections by default.
outbound.found.winFw: Windows Firewall blocks outgoing connections by default.
outbound.none.mac: No outbound firewall (such as LuLu or Little Snitch) controls which apps connect out.
outbound.none.win: No outbound firewall (such as simplewall, or Windows Firewall blocking outgoing connections by default) controls which apps connect out.
passwords.few: No profile holds more than {n}, so these are probably not your main passwords.
passwords.fewPass: {browsers} holds fewer than {n} saved passwords per profile: probably not your main passwords, so not counted.
passwords.fix: Move these passwords to a password manager (the browser's password settings can export them), delete them from the browser, and turn off saving.
passwords.fix.brave: Brave: Settings → Autofill and passwords → Password Manager → Settings → turn off Offer to save passwords.
passwords.fix.chrome: Chrome: Settings → Autofill and passwords → Google Password Manager → Settings → turn off Offer to save passwords.
passwords.fix.edge: Edge: Settings → Passwords and autofill (Profiles → Passwords in older versions) → turn off Offer to save passwords.
passwords.fix.firefox: Firefox: Settings → Privacy & Security → Passwords → uncheck Ask to save passwords.
passwords.fix.mac: On a Mac, Apple's Passwords app is a good choice: it is built in, unlocks with Touch ID, imports the file the browser exports, and fills in Chrome and Edge through Apple's iCloud Passwords extension.
passwords.fix.other: Other browsers: the password settings → turn off Offer to save passwords.
passwords.pass: No passwords are saved in the browsers, and they do not offer to save them.
passwords.passSavingOn: No passwords are saved in the browsers, but {browsers} still offers to save them: consider turning that off.
passwords.savingOn: {browsers} still offers to save passwords: consider turning that off.
passwords.stored: Passwords are saved in {browsers}. Information-stealing malware takes a browser's saved passwords first.

pm.checksum.one: 1 setting turns off Go's checksum database.
pm.checksum.other: {n} settings turn off Go's checksum database.

pm.fix.checksum: Turn Go's checksum database back on: [code]go env -u GOSUMDB GONOSUMDB[/code], and list only your company's module paths in GOPRIVATE ([code]go env -w GOPRIVATE=git.example.com/*[/code]), not [code]*[/code].
pm.fix.insecure: Use https:// registries and indexes, and remove settings that ignore certificate errors: [code]strict-ssl=false[/code] in ~/.npmrc, [code]trusted-host[/code] in pip.conf, [code]allow-insecure-host[/code] in uv.toml, [code]enableStrictSsl: false[/code] in ~/.yarnrc.yml; for Go run [code]go env -u GOINSECURE[/code]. If your company's own registry only speaks http, ask IT to add it to the policy's allow_hosts.
pm.fix.releaseAge: Wait a few days before installing a new version, so a hijacked release is caught first: npm 11.10+: [code]npm config set min-release-age 3[/code] (days); Bun: [code]minimumReleaseAge = 259200[/code] (seconds) under [install] in ~/.bunfig.toml; pnpm and Yarn: remove the line that sets [code]minimumReleaseAge[/code] or [code]npmMinimalAgeGate[/code] to 0.
pm.fix.scripts: Stop packages from running install scripts by default: [code]npm config set ignore-scripts true[/code] (run [code]npm rebuild PACKAGE[/code] for one that needs its script); pnpm: remove [code]dangerouslyAllowAllBuilds[/code]; Yarn: remove [code]enableScripts: true[/code] from ~/.yarnrc.yml.

pm.insecure.one: 1 setting fetches packages over plain http or ignores certificate errors.
pm.insecure.other: {n} settings fetch packages over plain http or ignore certificate errors.

prot.avOff: Microsoft Defender real-time protection is off and no other antivirus is on.
prot.fix.av: Windows Security → Virus & threat protection → Manage settings → turn on Real-time protection. If it turns itself off again, ask IT: a policy or malware may be switching it off.
prot.fix.gatekeeper: [code]sudo spctl --global-enable[/code], then System Settings → Privacy & Security → Allow applications from → App Store & Known Developers.
prot.fix.lsm: Ubuntu/Debian/openSUSE: [code]sudo systemctl enable --now apparmor[/code] (and remove apparmor=0 from the kernel command line). Fedora/RHEL: set [code]SELINUX=enforcing[/code] in /etc/selinux/config and restart.
prot.fix.secureBoot.linux: Enable Secure Boot in the firmware settings ([code]systemctl reboot --firmware-setup[/code]). Distributions with a signed shim (Ubuntu, Fedora, Debian…) boot as before; self-built kernels and extra modules (such as NVIDIA's) must be signed with a MOK first.
prot.fix.secureBoot.windows: Settings → System → Recovery → Advanced startup → Restart now → Troubleshoot → Advanced options → UEFI Firmware Settings, and enable Secure Boot there. With BitLocker on, have the recovery key at hand first.
prot.fix.selinux: [code]sudo setenforce 1[/code], and set [code]SELINUX=enforcing[/code] in /etc/selinux/config so it stays on after a restart.
prot.fix.sip: Start up in macOS Recovery (Apple silicon: hold the power button; Intel: Command-R), open Utilities → Terminal, run [code]csrutil enable[/code] and restart.
prot.fix.smartscreen: Windows Security → App & browser control → Reputation-based protection settings → turn on Check apps and files. If a policy sets it, ask IT.
prot.fix.tamper: Windows Security → Virus & threat protection → Manage settings → turn on Tamper Protection.
prot.gatekeeperOff: Gatekeeper is off: downloaded apps open without being checked for malware or a developer signature.
prot.noLSM: Neither AppArmor nor SELinux is active.
prot.note.noUEFI: This machine boots in legacy BIOS mode, which has no Secure Boot.
prot.note.unknown: Could not tell whether {what} is on.
prot.nothing: Nothing to check: every part of this check is turned off for this OS.
prot.secureBootOff: Secure Boot is off: malware can load before the OS starts.
prot.selinuxPermissive: SELinux is in permissive mode: it logs violations but blocks nothing.
prot.sipOff: System Integrity Protection is off: malware with administrator rights can change macOS itself and hide there.
prot.sipPartial: System Integrity Protection is only partly on (custom configuration).
prot.smartscreenOff: SmartScreen for apps and files is off: downloaded programs run without a reputation check.
prot.tamperOff: Microsoft Defender tamper protection is off: malware can switch Defender off.
prot.wsl: Windows Subsystem for Linux: Windows' own protections apply.
remote.fix.crd: Chrome Remote Desktop: if no one needs to reach this computer unattended, remove it on remotedesktop.google.com/access, or uninstall Chrome Remote Desktop Host.
remote.fix.linuxRDP: GNOME: Settings → System → Remote Desktop → turn off Desktop Sharing and Remote Login. xrdp: [code]sudo systemctl disable --now xrdp[/code].
remote.fix.linuxSSH: [code]sudo systemctl disable --now ssh.service ssh.socket[/code] (Debian/Ubuntu) or sshd.service (Fedora/Arch), or uninstall openssh-server.
remote.fix.linuxVNC: Turn off screen sharing (GNOME: Settings → Sharing; KDE: Krfb) and stop VNC servers such as x11vnc or TigerVNC.
remote.fix.macGuest: System Settings → Users & Groups → Guest User → turn off "Allow guests to log in to this computer".
remote.fix.macSharing: System Settings → General → Sharing → turn off {service}.
remote.fix.tool: {tool}: if it is not needed, quit it and uninstall it. Otherwise turn off its unattended access (permanent password) and its option to start with the system, and open it only while someone is at the computer.
remote.fix.winGuest: As administrator: Computer Management → Local Users and Groups → Users → Guest → tick "Account is disabled".
remote.fix.winRDP: Settings → System → Remote Desktop → Off (if a policy turned it on, ask IT).
remote.fix.winRM: As administrator: [code]winrm delete winrm/config/Listener?Address=*+Transport=HTTP[/code], then [code]Stop-Service WinRM; Set-Service WinRM -StartupType Disabled[/code].
remote.fix.winSSH: As administrator: [code]Stop-Service sshd; Set-Service sshd -StartupType Disabled[/code]. Or Settings → System → Optional features → remove OpenSSH Server.
remote.note.noSystemd: Could not read systemd unit states; judged from open ports only.

remote.tool.unattended: {tool} lets people connect without anyone at this computer approving: whoever has its unattended-access password, or the account it is linked to, controls this computer.
remote.tool.unattendedUnknown: Could not tell whether {tool} allows unattended access (a permanent password or an assigned account).

screenlock.fix.gnome.idle: Settings → Power → Screen Blank → the policy's limit or less, and Settings → Privacy & Security → Screen Lock → Automatic Screen Lock on.
screenlock.fix.gnome.password: Settings → Privacy & Security → Screen Lock → turn on Automatic Screen Lock and Lock Screen on Suspend, Automatic Screen Lock Delay → Screen Turns Off.
screenlock.fix.kde.idle: System Settings → Screen Locking → "Lock screen automatically" after the policy's limit or less.
screenlock.fix.kde.password: System Settings → Screen Locking → turn on "After waking from sleep".
screenlock.fix.macos.idle: System Settings → Lock Screen → set "Turn display off on battery when inactive" and "…on power adapter when inactive" (and "Start Screen Saver when inactive", if used) to the policy's limit or less.
screenlock.fix.macos.password: System Settings → Lock Screen → "Require password after screen saver begins or display is turned off" → Immediately.

secrets.chatGuard: To keep secrets out of Claude Code from now on (stop prompts that hold one, refuse commands that print them, hide them in commands' output), run [code]bordercheck guard install[/code].

secrets.chatInfo.one: For information: 1 secret in AI prompts or recent AI chat history ({files} file(s)). Run [code]bordercheck chats[/code] to check all of the history and see how to remove them.
secrets.chatInfo.other: For information: {n} secrets in AI prompts or recent AI chat history ({files} file(s)). Run [code]bordercheck chats[/code] to check all of the history and see how to remove them.

secrets.chatsPartial: AI chat history is larger than the policy's limit (checks.secrets.ai_chat_max_mb), so only its newest part was read.
secrets.fix.aiChat: For a key in an AI assistant's chat history, delete that conversation: the file listed holds it (Claude Code keeps each one as a .jsonl file under [code]~/.claude/projects[/code], Codex under [code]~/.codex/sessions[/code]; Gemini CLI, Copilot, Cursor's agent, Cline and Aider likewise keep one file per conversation or session). A prompt in a prompt history ([code]~/.claude/history.jsonl[/code], [code]~/.codex/history.jsonl[/code], [code].aider.input.history[/code]: what was typed) is one entry there: delete that entry. That removes the copy on this computer; the key was also sent to the assistant's provider. Claude Code deletes conversations older than [code]cleanupPeriodDays[/code] (30 by default, in [code]~/.claude/settings.json[/code]); a shorter period keeps fewer of them on disk.
secrets.fix.azureCache: Azure CLI keeps its sign-in tokens in plain text on macOS and Linux ([code]~/.azure/msal_token_cache.json[/code]; on Windows they are encrypted): run [code]az logout[/code] when you are done with Azure, and [code]az login[/code] again when you need it.
secrets.fix.azureLegacy: [code]~/.azure/accessTokens.json[/code] was written by an older Azure CLI, which current versions no longer read: run [code]az logout[/code], then delete the file.
secrets.fix.azureSP: Azure CLI keeps a service principal's secret in plain text after [code]az login --service-principal[/code]: run [code]az logout[/code] when done; where possible sign in with a certificate or a managed identity instead of a secret.
secrets.fix.docker: Let Docker keep logins in the system's store: in [code]~/.docker/config.json[/code] set [code]"credsStore"[/code] to [code]osxkeychain[/code] (macOS; Docker Desktop does this), [code]wincred[/code] (Windows) or [code]pass[/code] / [code]secretservice[/code] (Linux), then [code]docker logout[/code] and [code]docker login[/code] again.
secrets.fix.gcloudADC: Application default credentials hold a refresh token in plain text: [code]gcloud auth application-default revoke[/code] removes them; sign in again ([code]gcloud auth application-default login[/code]) only when a local tool needs them.
secrets.fix.gcloudKey: Keep a service account key file out of plain sight: store it in touchenv ([code]touchenv set NAME[/code], giving it the file as input), run tools with [code]touchenv run NAME:file -- …[/code] (the variable then holds a private temporary copy's path), and delete the file.
secrets.fix.gcloudStore: gcloud keeps its accounts' tokens in plain SQLite files: [code]gcloud auth revoke ACCOUNT[/code] removes an account you no longer use here ([code]gcloud auth list[/code] shows them).
secrets.fix.gh: Let GitHub CLI keep its token in the system keychain: [code]gh auth logout[/code], then [code]gh auth login[/code] (without [code]--insecure-storage[/code]).
secrets.fix.gitCreds: Let git keep passwords in the system's store: [code]git config --global credential.helper osxkeychain[/code] (macOS), [code]manager[/code] (Windows, Git Credential Manager) or [code]libsecret[/code] (Linux); then delete [code]~/.git-credentials[/code] and sign in again on the next push.
secrets.fix.kube: Let kubectl fetch short-lived tokens instead of keeping them in [code]~/.kube/config[/code]: use the cloud's exec plugin (EKS: [code]aws eks update-kubeconfig[/code], GKE: [code]gke-gcloud-auth-plugin[/code], AKS: [code]kubelogin[/code]) and remove the inline token or key.
secrets.fix.linux: Move each key into the desktop keyring ([code]secret-tool store[/code] / [code]secret-tool lookup[/code], from libsecret) or a password manager CLI such as pass or 1Password [code]op run[/code], then delete the line or file.
secrets.fix.mac: Move each key into the Keychain behind Touch ID with touchenv (https://github.com/ptrinh/touch-env): [code]touchenv set NAME[/code], then delete the line or file.
secrets.fix.other: Move each key into a password manager or the OS keyring, then delete the line or file.
secrets.fix.pgpass: Keep the password in touchenv and give it to the client only when it runs: [code]touchenv run PGPASSWORD -- psql …[/code]; then delete the line from [code].pgpass[/code].
secrets.fix.pypi: Upload with a PyPI API token kept out of the file: [code]touchenv run TWINE_PASSWORD -- twine upload …[/code] (with [code]TWINE_USERNAME=__token__[/code]), or the system keyring through the [code]keyring[/code] package; then remove the password from [code].pypirc[/code].
secrets.fix.rotate: For a key in shell history, deleting those lines is enough. Rotate a key only if there is evidence that this computer was compromised.
secrets.fix.terraform: [code]terraform logout[/code] removes the token; give it to Terraform when needed with [code]touchenv run TF_TOKEN_app_terraform_io -- terraform …[/code] (the variable is named after the host).
secrets.fix.win: Move each key into Windows Credential Manager or a password manager CLI (e.g. 1Password [code]op run[/code]), then delete the line or file.

sharing.fix.linuxNFS: [code]sudo systemctl disable --now nfs-server[/code] (nfs-kernel-server on Debian/Ubuntu), or limit each line of /etc/exports to named hosts, then [code]sudo exportfs -ra[/code].
sharing.fix.linuxSamba: Stop Samba if you don't need it: [code]sudo systemctl disable --now smbd[/code] (smb on Fedora). Otherwise remove [code]guest ok = yes[/code] and [code]public = yes[/code] from /etc/samba/smb.conf.
sharing.fix.macAirDrop: Control Center → AirDrop → Contacts Only (or turn AirDrop off), or in Finder: Go → AirDrop → "Allow me to be discovered by" → Contacts Only.
sharing.fix.macSharing: System Settings → General → Sharing → turn off {service}.
sharing.fix.winNearby: Settings → System → Nearby sharing → My devices only, or Off.
sharing.fix.winPrinters: Settings → Bluetooth & devices → Printers & scanners → the printer → Printer properties → Sharing → untick "Share this printer".
sharing.fix.winPublic: Settings → Network & internet → Advanced network settings → Advanced sharing settings → Public networks → turn off Network discovery and File and printer sharing; and set networks you don't own to Public.
sharing.fix.winShares: Stop sharing folders you don't need: as administrator, Computer Management → Shared Folders → Shares → right-click → Stop Sharing, or [code]Remove-SmbShare -Name SHARE[/code].
sharing.note.noSystemd: Could not read systemd unit states; judged from open ports only.
sharing.note.unknown: Could not tell whether {what} is on.
sharing.onOpen: {service} is on and lets anyone on the network in without a password.

sshkeys.authorized.one: 1 key in authorized_keys can log in to this machine.
sshkeys.authorized.other: {n} keys in authorized_keys can log in to this machine.

sshkeys.config.all.one: 1 setting in the SSH client config weakens every connection.
sshkeys.config.all.other: {n} settings in the SSH client config weaken every connection.

sshkeys.config.some.one: 1 setting in the SSH client config weakens connections to particular hosts.
sshkeys.config.some.other: {n} settings in the SSH client config weaken connections to particular hosts.

sshkeys.fix.config: In ~/.ssh/config, remove [code]ForwardAgent yes[/code] (use [code]ssh -A[/code] or [code]ProxyJump[/code] only where you need it: a server you forward your agent to can use your keys while you are logged in), and remove [code]StrictHostKeyChecking no[/code] and [code]UserKnownHostsFile /dev/null[/code] (use [code]StrictHostKeyChecking accept-new[/code] instead), so a server that suddenly has another key is noticed.
sshkeys.fix.mac: Let the Keychain remember the passphrase: [code]ssh-add --apple-use-keychain <key>[/code].
sshkeys.fix.passphrase: Add a passphrase: [code]ssh-keygen -p -f <key>[/code] (the key stays the same, nothing to re-upload), or move to a hardware key ([code]ssh-keygen -t ed25519-sk[/code]) or a password manager's SSH agent.
sshkeys.fix.rest: Make keys private: [code]chmod 600 <key>[/code]. Remove authorized_keys lines you don't recognise, and turn off the SSH server (Remote Login) if you don't use it.
sshkeys.fix.win: Let the Windows ssh-agent service hold the unlocked key: [code]ssh-add <key>[/code].

sshkeys.hardware.one: 1 hardware-backed key needs its token and is fine.
sshkeys.hardware.other: {n} hardware-backed keys need their token and are fine.

sshkeys.pass.one: 1 private key checked: it has a passphrase and private permissions; no authorized_keys.
sshkeys.pass.other: {n} private keys checked: all have a passphrase and private permissions; no authorized_keys.

sshkeys.readable.one: 1 key is readable by other users.
sshkeys.readable.other: {n} keys are readable by other users.

startup.downloadRun.one: 1 item downloads code and runs it each time it starts.
startup.downloadRun.other: {n} items download code and run it each time they start.

startup.fix.linux: Look up each item listed. If you don't recognise it, remove it: delete its .desktop file from ~/.config/autostart, [code]systemctl --user disable --now UNIT[/code], or [code]crontab -e[/code]. If one downloads and runs code, check the machine for malware; if you find any, change the passwords used on it.
startup.fix.mac: Look up each item listed. If you don't recognise it, remove it: [code]launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/LABEL[/code] and delete its .plist from ~/Library/LaunchAgents (items in /Library need an administrator); System Settings → General → Login Items & Extensions shows them too. If one downloads and runs code, run a malware scan; if it finds malware, change the passwords used on this Mac. Items whose program is gone are leftovers of uninstalled apps and can simply be removed.
startup.fix.win: Look up each item listed. If you don't recognise it, turn it off: Task Manager → Startup apps → Disable, Task Scheduler → the task → Disable, or delete its shortcut from the Startup folder ([code]shell:startup[/code]). If one downloads and runs code, run a full scan in Windows Security; if it finds malware, change the passwords used on this PC. Items whose program is gone are leftovers of uninstalled apps.

startup.missing.one: 1 item points to a program that no longer exists.
startup.missing.other: {n} items point to programs that no longer exist.

startup.pass.one: 1 item starts at login or on a schedule; nothing unusual.
startup.pass.other: {n} items start at login or on a schedule; nothing unusual.

startup.suspicious.one: 1 item starts a program from a temporary, download or hidden folder.
startup.suspicious.other: {n} items start programs from temporary, download or hidden folders.

startup.total.one: 1 item starts at login or on a schedule in all.
startup.total.other: {n} items start at login or on a schedule in all.

startup.writable.one: 1 item starts a program that any user can change.
startup.writable.other: {n} items start programs that any user can change.

tailscale.denied: Only root or the Tailscale operator may read Tailscale's settings here. Run [code]sudo tailscale set --operator=$USER[/code] once, or [code]sudo bordercheck -only mesh-vpn[/code]. ({err})
tailscale.open: Tailscale accepts incoming connections. Tailscale traffic may bypass the OS firewall, so any device on the tailnet, including a hacked one, can reach every port this machine listens on.
tailscale.open.fix: Tailscale → Settings → untick "Allow incoming connections". Or: [code]tailscale set --shields-up[/code]. Admins: also limit who can reach whom with tailnet ACLs.
tailscale.shieldsUp: Shields up: other devices on the tailnet cannot open connections to this machine.
tailscale.unreadable: Could not read Tailscale settings; is Tailscale running? ({err})
trust.ca.devTool: They include a development or debugging tool's certificate ({tools}): keep it only while you use the tool.

trust.ca.found.one: 1 root certificate was added to the trust store: {names}. Whoever holds its key can read this machine's HTTPS traffic that passes through them. Company TLS inspection and developer tools such as mkcert add one too.
trust.ca.found.other: {n} root certificates were added to the trust store: {names}. Whoever holds their keys can read this machine's HTTPS traffic that passes through them. Company TLS inspection and developer tools such as mkcert add them too.

trust.ca.hostOnly.one: 1 certificate is trusted for one host name only (such as a remote desktop's); not counted.
trust.ca.hostOnly.other: {n} certificates are trusted for one host name only (such as a remote desktop's); not counted.

trust.ca.unknown: The trust store could not be read: {err}
trust.fix.allow: If IT set this up, ask them to list it in the policy (allow_cas, allow_proxies).
trust.fix.ca.linux: Delete the file and rebuild the store: [code]sudo update-ca-certificates --fresh[/code] (Debian, Ubuntu) or [code]sudo update-ca-trust[/code] (Fedora, RHEL). For mkcert: [code]mkcert -uninstall[/code].
trust.fix.ca.mac: Keychain Access → login or System keychain → Certificates → double-click the certificate → Trust → When using this certificate: Use System Defaults, or delete it. For mkcert: [code]mkcert -uninstall[/code].
trust.fix.ca.win: Run [code]certmgr.msc[/code] → Trusted Root Certification Authorities → Certificates → right-click the certificate → Delete. For mkcert: [code]mkcert -uninstall[/code].
trust.fix.proxy.env: Remove http_proxy, https_proxy and all_proxy from your shell startup files or environment unless you set them up.
trust.fix.proxy.linux: Settings → Network → Network Proxy → turn it off, unless you set it up.
trust.fix.proxy.mac: System Settings → Network → your network → Details → Proxies → turn off the proxies you did not set up.
trust.fix.proxy.win: Settings → Network & internet → Proxy → turn off Use a proxy server and Use setup script unless you set them up.
trust.pass: No root certificates were added to the trust store, and no proxy is set.
trust.pass.ca: No root certificates were added to the trust store.
trust.proxy.found: Web traffic is sent through a proxy: {proxies}. A proxy you did not set up can see every site you visit and read unencrypted traffic.
trust.proxy.local: A proxy on this machine is set ({proxies}), usually a local tool such as a VPN client or a debugging proxy.
trust.proxy.unknown: The proxy settings could not be read: {err}
trust.unknown: Could not read the trust store or the proxy settings: {err}
tunnels.fix: Stop tunnels you aren't using ([code]tailscale funnel reset[/code], [code]tailscale serve reset[/code]; quit ngrok, [code]ssh -R[/code]…). If you must share something, use a named Cloudflare Tunnel behind Cloudflare Access, not a public URL.

tunnels.found.one: 1 tunnel publishes this machine beyond the local network.
tunnels.found.other: {n} tunnels publish this machine beyond the local network.

tunnels.pass: No tunnels publish this machine to the internet or the tailnet.

updates.autoOff.winService: The Windows Update service is disabled.
updates.autoUnknown: Could not tell whether automatic updates are on.

updates.belowMinWin: {os} is older than the minimum version build {min} set by policy.
updates.browserBelowMin: {browser} {version} is older than the minimum {min} set by policy.
updates.browserStale: {browser} has not updated for {days} days (policy: {max}); browsers ship security fixes every few weeks.
updates.checkStale: The OS last checked for updates {ago:ago} (policy: every {max} days).

updates.countWaitingLong.one: 1 update is waiting and nothing has been installed for {days} days (policy: {max}).
updates.countWaitingLong.other: {n} updates are waiting and nothing has been installed for {days} days (policy: {max}).

updates.fix.browser: Open each browser's About page (Chrome/Edge/Brave: Settings → About; Firefox: Help → About Firefox) to update it, then relaunch it; uninstall browsers you don't use.
updates.fix.debian.auto: [code]sudo apt install unattended-upgrades && sudo dpkg-reconfigure -plow unattended-upgrades[/code]
updates.fix.debian.reboot: Restart to finish installing updates (/var/run/reboot-required is set).
updates.fix.debian.upgrade: Upgrade to a supported release (Ubuntu: [code]sudo do-release-upgrade[/code]).
updates.fix.fedora.auto: [code]sudo dnf install dnf-automatic[/code], set [code]apply_updates = yes[/code] in /etc/dnf/automatic.conf, then [code]sudo systemctl enable --now dnf-automatic.timer[/code] (dnf5-automatic.timer on dnf5).
updates.fix.fedora.upgrade: Upgrade to a supported release: [code]sudo dnf system-upgrade[/code] (see the Fedora upgrade guide).
updates.fix.generic: Install the latest updates with your distribution's package manager, and restart.
updates.fix.macos.auto: System Settings → General → Software Update → Automatic updates (i) → turn on Check for updates, Download new updates when available and Install Security Responses and system files.
updates.fix.macos.check: Connect to the internet and open System Settings → General → Software Update so macOS checks again.
updates.fix.macos.pending: System Settings → General → Software Update → Update Now.
updates.fix.macos.upgrade: System Settings → General → Software Update → upgrade to a supported macOS.
updates.fix.windows.auto: Windows Update must run automatically: the Windows Update service (wuauserv) must not be Disabled and no policy may turn automatic updates off. If Settings → Windows Update says some settings are managed by your organisation, ask IT.
updates.fix.windows.check: Settings → Windows Update → Check for updates.
updates.fix.windows.pending: Settings → Windows Update → Check for updates, install everything, then restart.
updates.fix.windows.reboot: Restart the PC to finish installing updates.
updates.fix.windows.upgrade: Settings → Windows Update → install the latest Windows 11 feature update.
updates.noneInstalled: No OS update has been installed for {days} days (policy: {max}).
updates.note.gnomeSoftware: GNOME Software downloads updates; they install on restart.
updates.note.macSettings: Could not read Software Update's settings.
updates.note.winLastInstall: Could not read when Windows last installed an update.
updates.reboot: Updates are installed but need a restart to take effect.
updates.stateAutoChecked: {os}, automatic updates on, last checked for updates {ago:ago}.
updates.waitingLong: {name} has been waiting to be installed for {days} days (policy: {max}).
